symptom:
A small TCP key-value server (server/main.go) appends every PUT as a checksummed key=value line to data/kv.log, fsyncs, and only then answers OK. On start it reads the log back, verifies each record and rebuilds its in-memory map. The client remembers every PUT that was answered OK and reads them all back at the end. If the last record of the log is incomplete after a crash, recovery cuts it off and carries on appending.

Observed on seed 1: the server was crashed four times, three of them in the middle of a disk operation (ops 56, 94 and 106). After the last crash the restarted server exited at startup with: data/kv.log: the record at offset 722 fails its checksum in 40 reads, and the run failed with: server#5 crashed: module closed with exit_code(1). It had been serving 43 keys before that.

Expected: after any sequence of crashes, including crashes in the middle of a write, the server must start again and every PUT that returned OK must be readable.
